Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement

Hello Morgan State University Faculty & Staff, In this module, we will review key post-award processes for travel on sponsored projects at Morgan State University. Topics include processing travel request forms, requesting reimbursement of travel-related expenses, guidelines for group travel, and more. Please note that the processes detailed in this module are specific to grant-funded activities. Some of the information may also be relevant to state-funded budget actions; however, policy and procedural differences may apply. Review the Travel Office website for further clarification. We strive to continuously review these lessons to provide up-to-date guidance on Morgan’s sponsored project processes. For questions related to the activities covered in this module that are not addressed in the module content, please contact the ORA Training and Communications Coordinator: Mr. Ryan Mobley, CRA, CFRA, CPRA Email: ryan.mobley@morgan.edu Phone: 443-885-4771 Thank you, ORA Training Team

## Things to Know: Prior to Travel Request
Greetings MSU Faculty and Staff!
Traveling on grant funding is a valuable opportunity to expand your research network, collaborate with leading experts, and gain exposure to cutting-edge practices in your field. Before we jump into travel procedures for MSU-organized travel please review the important information below.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Things to Know: Prior to Travel Form Submission
Destination details & allocability
Where are you going on the trip? How long will you be there? Why are you going there? Is this travel related to your project's scope of work?
Estimated Expenses
Think about what costs you will incur over the course of this trip: Conference registration fees Hotel/Lodging Flight or Train ticket Meal costs per diem Please Note: You cannot claim per diem for meals offered by a conference while on University travel. When submitting reimbursement, MSU's travel office will compare requested per diem reimbursements with conference itineraries to determine allowability. Ground Transportation (personal vehicle mileage, taxi/uber, tolls, hotel/airport parking, etc)
Index & Budget
Be sure to use the correct Banner index on travel forms, as provided by the RFA team at project setup. Also, check your budget to ensure you have enough funds in the 04: Travel pool.
p-card Purchases
Many travel expenses may be charged to your University Purchasing Card, helping to minimize the need for out-of-pocket payments and reduce reliance on travel reimbursements. Such expenses may include: Conference Registration Fees Hotel/Lodging Uber/Taxi Parking

## Booking a Flight or Train Ticket
Flight & Train Costs
Travel Form (TL) Required
A Travel Authorization (TL) Form is required to book a flight or train ticket. Please submit with enough lead time to allow for form approval and processing. The steps to submit a TL form are outlined later in this module.
Using Globetrotter
Globetrotter (1-888-337-2462) is the State of Maryland travel agency. We must utilize Globetrotter to book any flight or train ticket needed on University travel. Call them to get a quote for your flight so you have a reasonable estimate of the expected flight cost. You may also look up your preferred flight online to estimate your flight costs.
Traveler Info
When calling Globetrotter to book a flight be sure you have the traveler's full legal name, birthdate, and contact phone number. Additionally, collect frequent flier or reward account numbers from the traveler so they are applied to the fare.
Fly America Act
The Fly America Act (49 USC 40118) requires federally funded travelers to use US flag air carriers whenever possible, even when cheaper options are available. Make sure you verify this act is adhered to by Globetrotter when making arrangements.
Baggage Fees
Check with your chosen airline to determine what baggage fees may apply for your flight. Any such charges should be included under "Portage" on the MSU Travel Form.

An American Airlines ticket will cost $750 while an Icelandic Air flight will only cost $390. The PI wants to use the Icelandic Air flight to save money for their grant. Is this allowable?
  - Yes  [incorrect]
  - No  [CORRECT ANSWER]

  If incorrect: Remember the Fly America Act? When using federal funds we must use American-operated airlines.
  Note on "Yes": Great Job! Due to the Fly America Act we must choose an American-operated airline even when they may be the more expensive option.
  Note on "No": Remember the Fly America Act? We must use American carriers when traveling using federal funds.

## Group Travel Guidance
Group Travel Rules
There are times when a single faculty member or administrative employee may lead a group of students to a conference or event. In such cases, one travel request form may be submitted under the employee’s name, with an attached Attendees List (see below) of all student participants. Additional group travel guidelines are outlined below.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Group Travel Attendees List
Required Attendee List
A completed Attendee List is required for group travel requests. This document must be completed and submitted as supporting documentation for the travel authorization or reimbursement form.
No Reimbursements
Students that are on group travel are not able to submit a travel reimbursement for travel expenses. If you believe reimbursement will be necessary, please complete separate TL requests for each student on the trip.
Graduate Student Restriction
Graduate students cannot receive funding from the GSA (Graduate Student Association) for any travel covered by other funding.
Travel Advances
Faculty/Staff running a group travel can request travel advances for the student attendees. The check will be made out in the employee's name, and that employee will be responsible for disbursing advances to students that require it. Further information on travel advances can be found on the Comptroller's Travel Office page.

## Additional Travel Rules
Supplemental Travel Policies
Hotel & Other Lodging
Travel destination must be more than 40 miles from MSU campus for lodging expenses to be allowable. AirBNB is prohibited. Tax charges & lodging fees are allowed for hotel/lodging expenses. If the traveler does not have a University Purchasing Card at check-in, an admin with a p-card tied to your grant must submit a Credit Card Authorization Form prior to your stay. Check with your chosen hotel for further details. Hotel housekeeping tips will be reimbursed up to $1 per day. Travelers are responsible for all incidental charges, including room service and streaming options. Incidental charges are not allowed to be charged to either a grant or state-fund.
Car Rental
Do not purchase additional insurance (MSU has basic coverage). Rental contracts should be signed "Traveler Name, Morgan State University, State of Maryland" to be covered by MSU. It is encouraged to use Globetrotter for car rental, but not mandatory.
Uber/Taxi
Keep original receipts for any taxi fare. Tips should be limited to no more than 20% of the total fare cost. These costs should be listed under "ground transportation" on the TL form.
International Travel
International travel is commonly not allowable on grants unless permission is granted by the sponsor via the Notice of Award (NOA) or written notification. When submitting international travel request forms, be sure to include a copy of your project's NOA as supporting documentation.

Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: A psychology professor plans to attend the 2025 American Psychological Association (APA) Conference with their Co-Principal Investigator. While the conference hotel charges $250 per night for a single room, the professor identified an Airbnb that can accommodate both attendees for $300 per night. Is the professor permitted to choose the more cost-effective Airbnb option?
  - Yes  [incorrect]
  - No  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: While it may appear more cost-effective, university policy does not allow Airbnb accommodations due to liability and risk management concerns.

## Travel Request Form (TL Form) Guidance
MSU Travel Authorization Forms
Completing a Travel Request (TL) form is a mandatory step in the university’s travel process. It ensures that Morgan State University is aware of travel plans, enabling proper documentation and coordination. Submitting a TL form also activates necessary insurance coverage for MSU travelers and allows departments to address any coverage considerations for faculty traveling during the academic year. Please review the guidance below for best practices on completing your travel requests.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Completing a Travel Request (TL) Form
Grant-Funded Travel must utilize the ORA Travel DocuSign forms found here . All Out-of-State travel requires an authorized TL form.
sm
Travel Advances
If needed, travel advances must be requested no less than 30 days prior to travel. Please review guidance on this from the Office of the Comptroller here .
Amended Travel
If you are submitting a corrected/amended travel form please include the previously approved travel authorization number (TL#) here.
Traveler Information
Please enter all traveler information here.
Email Copy
There is room to add a second email address on a separate line, if someone other than the traveler needs a copy of the completed TL form.
Method of Travel
Select the primary method of travel used on the trip. Flight and train tickets should be booked through Globetrotter .
International Travel
Traveling outside of the US is generally not allowed on grants without explicit permission from the sponsor. If allowable, international travel requires approval from the EVP for Finance and Management.
Banner Index
The 6-digit code requested here should match your project's Banner index. This number is shared by the Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) team during initial award setup.
Banner Account Code
This five digit number refers to the Banner account code used for travel expenses. They are as follows: 04010: In State Routine Travel 04020: In State Conference 04030: Out of State Routine Travel 04040: Out of State Conference 04041: Out of Country Travel
MSU ID
Enter the MSU ID of the traveler.
Total Estimated Costs
In this column the initiator should detail all expected costs of the travel. It is best to pad the flight cost slightly to allow for potential cost increases during travel-form processing. Meal per diem rates can be found on the Comptroller's site here . Per diem is based on travel times. For example, if you leave for the trip around 1 pm you wouldn't be able to claim breakfast per diem that day. "Other Transportation" would cover costs such as mileage, tolls, parking, and taxi.
P-Card or Purchase Order Expenses
Any expense paid for by p-card or purchase order should be accounted for in this column. These charges will reduce the total funds held in column #3 (Total to be Encumbered).
Total Encumbered
The ORA Grant-funded Travel Request (TL) Form will automatically calculate the amount that needs to be encumbered in this 3 rd column. Funds encumbered will be set aside, i.e. “committed”, for the Banner Index listed on this form in Pool Level 04. The total amount set aside, $1,028, includes $400 for airfare and the remaining balance for meal and ground transportation reimbursements upon your return. Figures in this column should never be negative.

Additional TL Form Information
Form Submission Timeline
Travel requests should be submitted no later than 30 days prior to departure for domestic travel and 90 days for international travel. A travel form requires multiple approvals and review from various departments on campus to include your department's administration, ORA, and the MSU Travel Office.
Required Supporting Documentation
When submitting a travel request you need to provide supporting documentation that matches your estimated expenses. Such required documents may include: Hotel Booking Confirmation Conference Registration fee receipt/invoice Mileage Map (if using personal vehicle) Notice of Award (for international travel)
In-State Travel Guidance
Not all in-state travel will require a travel authorization form. However, you will need to submit one if: Hotel/Lodging expenses are expected for the trip A travel advance will be needed You need to use Globetrotter for a train ticket or other transportation The traveler is a non-MSU (external) individual using Globetrotter for accommodations In-State travel authorization forms are subject to the EVP for Finance and Management's review. Washington DC is considered "in-state." Lodging is an allowable cost if the meeting/conference destination is at least 40 miles from MSU campus.
Meal Per Diem
Per diem rates for meals can vary widely by destination. The standard rates for in-state travel, and travel to lower-cost destinations, are listed on the Comptoller's page here . The current rates are: $15 for Breakfast $18 for Lunch $30 for Dinner High-cost metropolitan areas such as NYC or Miami will typically have a greater per diem allowance than the standard meal allowance listed on the Comptroller's Travel page. Consider the per diem rates found here when planning a trip out of state to ensure you utilize the appropriate rate. Per diem rates change annually so be sure you are using current figures.

## Travel Reimbursement Form (GAD Form X-5)
How To: Completing a Travel Reimbursement Form
Grant-Funded Travelers should use the Travel Reimbursement Form DocuSign found here .
sm
When to Submit
Reimbursement requests should be submitted within 5 business days of the traveler's return.
Expenses to Include
On this form make sure to only include on this form those expenses which need to be reimbursed. Expenses paid by purchase order or p-card should not be listed on the reimbursement form.
Commute Miles
The form requires entry of commute miles if you are requesting mileage reimbursement. Total mileage reimbursement will be reduced by the traveler's commute mileage on travel days when they would typically work (commonly Monday - Friday).
Meal Per Diem
Receipts are not required for meal per diem reimbursement. A traveler can only request per diem based on their travel times. For example, here John Doe left his home at 12:30pm and does not qualify for breakfast on Tuesday July 1st. Review the travel guidance on per diem rates covered in the "How to Complete a TL Form" lesson in this module.
Meal Per Diem (In-State Travel)
If traveling in-state, a traveler can only request per diem if they leave their home 2 hours earlier than usual AND return home 2 hours later than usual.
Taxi Reimbursement
Taxi and rideshare charges can be reimbursed if receipts are provided to the MSU Travel Office. Tips will be reimbursed up to 20% of the total fare cost.
Mileage Reimbursement
Mileage reimbursement is automatically calculated based on figures entered on the second table of this form. The mileage rate changes every fiscal year. A mileage map is required for mileage reimbursement requests. See example below in this lesson.
Total Reimbursement
The total amount to be reimbursed to the traveler is listed here ($478.11). This figure may be reduced by the Travel Office if a travel advance was requested. If the advance exceeds the total reimbursement the difference must be returned to the Bursar's Office.
Travel Times
Travel times are important for several reasons. The University needs to know when the traveler is covered by MSU's insurance. It is also vital in per diem calculations.
Commute Miles (Continued)
As mentioned above, mileage reimbursement requests do not need to factor in commute mileage if it is a non-standard working day. In our example, John came back from travel on Sunday so he is entitled to the full mileage reimbursement.
Agency Code
Morgan State University's Agency Code is 36.13.00. You will use this code for any MSU-funded travel reimbursement.

Supporting Documentation for Reimbursement

Most reimbursement requests should be accompanied by an authorized TL form. One exception exists: in-state travel without lodging expenses. In that case, include the 6-digit budget index and travel account code (04XXX) on the reimbursement form.
Authorized TL Form
If you are requesting mileage reimbursement. A printout of Google Maps or MapQuest works fine.
Mileage Map
You will need original receipts if requesting reimbursement of expenses such as hotel, parking fees, tolls, taxi/rideshare, baggage fees, etc. Receipts are not needed for meal per diem expenses.
Original Receipts
If you request reimbursement for out-of-pocket expenses you may be required to submit a redacted copy of your personal card statement. The statement must include your name, address, last 4 digits of card used, and expense detail.
Redacted Credit Card Statement
Only for group travel activity. If applicable, please note the travel advance provided to each student.
Attendee List
Only if a travel advance was requested by the traveler.
Check Stub
The State of Maryland now requires a travel itinerary for each reimbursement request. Either (a) a self drafted itinerary of travel times/events or (b) a conference-supplied itinerary is appropriate.
